correctness.rationale: A direct binomial computation gives every endpoint matrix entry; the absorbing generator column gives a separate weighted-exponential polynomial. All odd-degree critical polynomials have unique roots by strict derivative negativity and positive even truncations. This establishes the exact closed feasible interval and non-reentry. Root monotonicity proves all three sharp dimension staircase identities; endpoint Laplace/Stirling estimates prove both fixed-dimension limits. Exact rational code independently verifies finite p,d examples; no finite computation is used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The bDeC common Taylor stability polynomial (Micalizzi–Torlo Theorem 2) and classical exponential partial-sum zero asymptotics are pre-existing. The assessed new statement is the all-order, all-chain-length exact endpoint-stochasticity threshold on equal-rate absorbing pure-birth chains, its dimension staircase and parity-sensitive fixed-dimension high-order limits. Direct full-text comparisons with the primary method paper and Horváth show distinct domains of stated results; equivalent hidden absolute-monotonicity/Jordan formulations remain a risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent special-case theorem could appear as a corollary in older absolute-monotonicity/Jordan-block literature without the same Markov-chain terminology.
Not all relevant Patankar and exponential-partial-sum references were fully text-inspected; they are distinguished by method and already credited for component results.
Fixed-dimension p-asymptotics do not extend to dimensions growing with p without further analysis.

value.rationale: The question is the exact mass-preserving/nonnegative step-size range for an established high-order explicit DeC family on a natural finite-state pure-birth Markov benchmark. The result is the complete necessary-and-sufficient all-dimension classification plus sharp dimension staircase and distinct high-order scaling constants; scalar stability analysis and method-wide SSP restrictions alone do not provide this fine-grained information. It supplies usable step-size barriers and clarifies the need for nonlinear positivity modifications.
